items.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: I worked with Leith Stevens on a couple of things

ctx.x: Did you do much writing for the studios as far as the film music and—

I did some in the ‘50s when they were using a lot of jazz scores, and especially a lot of T.V. shows. I worked with Leith Stevens on a couple of things, who was a very good Hollywood picture film composer. I’ve never gone into actually composing for movies. I did a couple of grade C movies in the ‘50s.

items.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Leith Stevens had done the music for that picture. They were all his themes, and I just made arrangements out of them

ctx.x: Then here‟s one that seems to be significant: The James Dean Story. Chet Baker and Bud Shank, listed as the leaders on this one. It‟s a film soundtrack, November of ‟56. You‟re credited with arranging Fairmount Indiana, Let Me Be Loved, The Movie Star, Lost Love, Hollywood. So this film soundtrack for The James Dean Story.
Leith Stevens had done the music for that picture. They were all his themes, and I just made arrangements out of them for a medium-sized jazz band.

Then here‟s a very interesting one: Ray Brown with Marty Paich‟s orchestra. Bass Hit is the title, from November of ‟56. A killer band: Harry “Sweets” Edison, Peter Candoli, Herb Geller, yourself, Jimmy Giuffre, Jimmy Rowles, Herb Ellis, Ray Brown, Alvin Stoller, Marty Paich. When you‟ve got folks like that, I was just wondering, was that a magical session, when you bring folks like that together? There were only four or five titles done. There were several takes of After You‟ve Gone though.
